rv.q: Strong individual performances, particularly Henri Lubatti’s tantrum-prone king, anchor the production, but overall it lacks the fever-dream energy necessary to fully ignite Ionesco’s absurdist vision.
Kudos to A Noise Within for offering an opportunity to experience this work in a remarkable, potentially even life-changing, way.
Exit the King reaches some of life’s most profound and vexing dilemmas by a circuitous route through the absurd to the paradox of human existence.
I encourage audiences to head to Pasadena to check out this play that deals equal measures of drama and comedy.
It’s in the final moments, when kingdom’s shabby palatial hall transforms to a cavernous cosmic space, that the message of the playwright is powerfully brought home.
For this reviewer, at least, it ends up being just one out of two.
This fine production of a very important piece of absurdist theatre needs to be seen and appreciated at an antidote for our time.

cn.t: Ionesco's absurdist meditation on mortality divides critics, with strong performances (particularly Lubatti) and design praised, but some find the existential premise tedious despite committed direction and production values.
